title: Narrative writing
examples: How do I make the beginning of my story exciting?
What is the best way to write conversations between characters?
Can you show me how to build suspense in a story?

explain.say: Today we are learning about narrative writing techniques. We will look at story structure first. Story structure helps your story have a clear beginning middle and end.

items: End: Resolve the conflict and conclude

explain.say: Next we will explore building tension in your writing. Tension keeps the reader wanting to know what happens next. You can build it by delaying important information.
Our third point is using effective dialogue. Dialogue is what your characters actually say to each other. It helps show personality and move the plot forward.
For a concrete example of structure, think of a mystery novel. The beginning sets the scene with a puzzle. The middle has clues found. The end reveals the culprit.

items: The missing item is found | The detective questions suspects | The thief is caug

explain.say: To build tension, imagine a character waiting for a phone call. You can describe their anxious pacing and checking the clock. This makes us wait with them.
In real life, think about a tense argument between friends. Their words create dialogue. The way they speak builds tension. The resolution shows the structure.

faq.q: How long should my story be to show good structure?
faq.a: There is no set length for structure. A short story can have a clear beginning middle and end. You just need to make sure the plot moves through those three parts.
asks: What is the ideal length for a narrative?
Do I need many paragraphs for structure?

faq.q: What is the difference between tension and conflict?
faq.a: Conflict is the main problem in the story. Tension is the feeling of suspense around that problem. Tension makes the reader feel nervous while the conflict is happening.
asks: Are tension and conflict the same thing?
How do I show tension without telling the reader?

faq.q: When should I use dialogue in my story?
faq.a: You should use dialogue when characters are speaking to each other. It is best used during the middle section to reveal character or advance the plot.
asks: Is dialogue only for talking parts?
Can I start a story with dialogue?

faq.q: If I write a lot of dialogue, will my story still have structure?
faq.a: Yes, dialogue can move the structure along. Make sure the conversation leads to a change, like a decision or a realization, to keep the structure moving.
asks: Does dialogue count as plot development?
How much dialogue is too much?

faq.q: How can I make the beginning really gripping?
faq.a: Start in the middle of an action or right before something important happens. This technique immediately grabs the reader's attention and starts the tension.
asks: What is a good opening hook?
Should I describe the setting first?

facts: A narrative typically includes a beginning, a middle, and an end.
Tension is built by creating suspense or anticipation for an event.
Dialogue should sound like real speech for believable characters.
Show, do not tell, is a key writing technique for vivid description.

quiz.say: A story that introduces characters and setting, builds action, and then resolves the main problem follows what pattern?
quiz.why: This sequence describes the standard narrative arc from setup to climax to resolution.

wrong.1: This skips the necessary introduction of characters and the initial problem setup.
wrong.2: These are elements, not the required structural sequence of the story.
wrong.3: While tension and dialogue are important, they are techniques used within the structure, not the structure itself.

quiz.say: To make a reader feel anxious about what happens next, a writer should:

options.show: Describe the character waiting anxiously for the results.
options.say: Describe the character waiting anxiously for the results.

options.show: Simply stating the results are bad.
options.say: Simply stating the results are bad.

options.show: Writing a long description of the room.
options.say: Writing a long description of the room.

options.show: Having the characters talk about the weather.
options.say: Having the characters talk about the weather.

quiz.why: Describing the waiting action builds suspense, which is the core of tension.

wrong.1: Telling the reader the outcome removes all suspense and tension.
wrong.2: This is setting detail and does not inherently create emotional suspense.
wrong.3: This is irrelevant detail that distracts from building the necessary emotional tension.

quiz.say: When writing a conversation, the words spoken by the characters are called:
quiz.why: Dialogue refers specifically to the spoken exchange between two or more characters.

wrong.0: Narration is the writer's voice describing the action, not what the characters say.
wrong.1: Description uses adjectives and adverbs to paint a picture, not to convey speech.
wrong.2: Exposition is background information given to the reader, not direct speech.
